To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GAPDH is induced by cobalt, nickel manganese, and deferoxamine and that GAPDH induction is blocked by cyclo-heximide.
GAPDH is induced by hypoxic exposure of endothelial cells, and that this induction is regulated by a pathway that is different from that of other hypoxic genes.
hypoxia induces the expression of GAPDH in endothelial cells, and that this response is mediated by the activation of a protein kinase that is not inhibited by the inhibitors of heme synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which hypoxia induces the glycolytic enzyme, glyceraldehyde- 3-phosphate dehydrgenase (GAPD) in endothelial cells.
the regulation of gene expression by hypoxia and with the role of the glycolytic enzyme GAPDH in the response of cells to hypoxia.
the regulation of endothelial cell function by hypoxia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GAPDH is a hypoxia-inducible protein in EC.

the hypoxic induction of the glycolytic enzyme GAPDH in EC involves a mechanism that is independent of the heme-regulated oxygen sensor, that is independent of protein kinase and calcium signaling pathways, that requires protein synthesis, and that may be mediated, in part, by nitric oxide.
the induction of GAPDH in EC by hypoxia occurs via mechanisms other then those that are involved in other hypoxic responsive systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GAPDH is a hypoxia-responsive protein, and that its regulation occurs via mechanisms distinct from those involved in the regulation of other hypoxa-inducible genes.
GAPDH is regulated at the posttranscriptional level by hypoxia and that this regulation is independent of the hypoxia-responsive element.

GAPDH induction in EC is mediated by a novel pathway that involves the transcription of a new mRNA species and that is not inhibited by CO, is independent of heme, is not mediated by nitric oxide, is not mediated through the redox state of the cell, and is not dependent on protein synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GAPDH induction in response to hypoxia is a novel and unique response in EC.
the regulation of GAPDH by hypoxia is not mediated by any of the known pathways of hypoxia response.
the induction of the glycolytic enzyme GAPDH by hypoxia occurs via a mechanism that is distinct from that of other hypoxic-responsive systems.
